**Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.** Did It Work? is a tenant system on it (level 1, parent `ultrastable`).

Every big policy promised something. See what it promised, what the evaluations found since, and how the verdict moved.

Idea and system test: `IDEA.md`. Who it is and where it runs: `ultrastable.json`. Manifest: `instance.json`. What could stop it within a year and the safeguard for each: `runway.json`.

| Piece | Code |
|---|---|
| Router, the beat and `/health` | `worker/index.js` |
| Pages (server-rendered, readable without script) | `worker/site.js` |
| What the site states, the page that shows each statement and the endpoint that backs it | `worker/contract.js`, served at `/claims.json` |
| Published cases | `worker/entries.js`, served at `/api/entries.json` |
| Core files, vendored and refreshed daily | `vendor/ultrastable/` |
| Tests | `npm test` |

Source of the platform: <https://github.com/ultrastable/ultrastable>.

## How this system runs

**What it is.** Every big policy promised something. See what it promised, what the evaluations found since, and how the verdict moved.

**The loop it closes.** A daily beat searches open evaluation and trial registries for each case, adds new evaluations, re-grades the verdict when evidence piles up, and logs every change of verdict with its reason.

**How it bootstraps.** It is a tenant of the platform ([ultrastable/ultrastable](https://github.com/ultrastable/ultrastable)): its manifest is registered there, this repository holds its code, and the platform builds this repository's `main` into its Worker.
<!-- how:end -->
